title: Arithmetic roots of the integral factors
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$ and
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, and geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Fix indeterminates $T$ and $U$. For every
prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and, for
$P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for coefficientwise extension, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Fix an integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$. Let
$P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the
integral Frobenius factor
with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell\neq p$,
and put $r_i=\deg P_i$. Fix an algebraic closure
$\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$. A
reciprocal root
$\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $P_i$ means a root of
$P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}P_i(U^{-1})$; its inverse $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ is the
corresponding ordinary root.
The reciprocal polynomial

$$
P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}P_i(U^{-1})\in\mathbf Z[U]
$$

is monic, and every reciprocal root $\alpha$ is an
algebraic integer. For every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$,

$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2};
$$

and $\alpha$ is a
$q$-Weil number of weight $i$. More
explicitly, for every prime $\ell'\neq p$, let
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$ be an algebraic closure of
$\mathbf Q_{\ell'}$, set

$$
\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell')}=
\{z\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}:z\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\},
$$

and choose an
ell-adic realization
$\jmath_{\ell'}:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell')}$. Then $\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is a reciprocal root
of $P_{i,\ell'}$, hence an eigenvalue of $F_{i,\ell'}$ on
$H^i(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'})$, the
ordinary cohomology group
after scalar extension.
Every ordinary root $\beta$
satisfies,
for every $\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$,

$$
|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}.
$$

proof.text: *Step 1: the reciprocal polynomial.* The hypotheses on $P_i$ are those of the statement: $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $P_i(0)=1$, $r_i=\deg P_i$, and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every prime $\ell\neq p$, in the sense of [def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor]; they are used as hypotheses (no existence or uniqueness result about $P_i$ is needed). Apply [lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial] to $P_i$ over $R=\mathbf Z$: $P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}P_i(U^{-1})=\sum_k c_kU^{r_i-k}$ lies in $\mathbf Z[U]$, is monic of degree $r_i$, and $P_i^\#(0)$ is the leading coefficient of $P_i$, which is nonzero. Moreover, for every field $K$ of characteristic $0$ (below $K=\overline{\mathbf Q}$ and $K=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$) and every $x\in K$: $(P_i^\#)^{(K)}(x)=0$ if and only if $x\neq0$ and $P_i^{(K)}(x^{-1})=0$. Hence every reciprocal root $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $P_i$ (a root of $P_i^\#$) is nonzero, its inverse $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ is a root of $P_i$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}$, and conversely the inverse of every root of $P_i$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ is a reciprocal root. So the ordinary roots of the statement are exactly the roots of $P_i$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}$, and the statement's convention is that of [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots] with $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ in place of $\Qlb$. This proves that $P_i^\#$ is monic.

source.place: ## Proof, 'By [prop-integral-recovery], the polynomial $P_i$ is integral ... so the reversed polynomial is monic'

proof.text: *Step 2: reciprocal roots are algebraic integers.* Let $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ be a reciprocal root of $P_i$. By Step 1, $P_i^\#\in\mathbf Z[U]$ is monic of degree $r_i$ and $P_i^\#(\alpha)=0$; a nonzero constant has no root, so $r_i\geq1$. Writing $P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}+a_{r_i-1}U^{r_i-1}+\cdots+a_1U+a_0$ with $a_k\in\mathbf Z$, the equation $P_i^\#(\alpha)=0$ reads $\alpha^{r_i}+a_{r_i-1}\alpha^{r_i-1}+\cdots+a_1\alpha+a_0=0$, which is the algebraic-integer condition of [def-weil-numbers] with $m=r_i$. Hence $\alpha$ is an algebraic integer.

source.place: ## Proof, 'so the reversed polynomial is monic and its roots are algebraic integers' and 'The terminology and algebraic-integer criterion are those of [def-weil-numbers]'

proof.text: *Step 3: the realization $\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is a reciprocal root of $P_{i,\ell'}$.* Fix a prime $\ell'\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$ of $\mathbf Q_{\ell'}$, and an $\ell'$-adic realization $\jmath=\jmath_{\ell'}:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell')}\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$ in the sense of [def-weil-algebraic-closure-q]; composed with the inclusion, $\jmath$ is a ring homomorphism of fields $\overline{\mathbf Q}\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$. Let $\alpha$ be a reciprocal root of $P_i$, so $P_i^\#(\alpha)=0$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ (coefficients extended along $\mathbf Z\to\overline{\mathbf Q}$). By [lem-weil-polynomial-root-ring-hom] applied to $P_i^\#\in\mathbf Z[U]$ and $\jmath$, one gets $(P_i^\#)^{(\ell')}(\jmath(\alpha))=0$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$, where $(\cdot)^{(\ell')}$ is the coefficientwise extension $\mathbf Z\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$. By [lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial] applied with $K=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$ (characteristic $0$), $\jmath(\alpha)\neq0$ and $P_i^{(\ell')}(\jmath(\alpha)^{-1})=0$. By hypothesis ([def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor]) $P_i^{(\ell')}=P_{i,\ell'}$ in $\mathbf Q_{\ell'}[T]\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}[T]$, and $P_{i,\ell'}(0)=1$ by [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]. Thus $P_{i,\ell'}(\jmath(\alpha)^{-1})=0$ with $\jmath(\alpha)\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}^{\times}$: by [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], $\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is a reciprocal root of $P_{i,\ell'}$.

source.place: statement, 'Then $\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is a reciprocal root of $P_{i,\ell'}$' (the ## Proof gives no argument; written out here)

proof.text: *Step 4: $\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is an eigenvalue of Frobenius on $H^i(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'})$.* Keep $\ell'$, $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$ and $\jmath_{\ell'}$ as in Step 3. By [prop-weil-reciprocal-roots-eigenvalues], the reciprocal roots of $P_{i,\ell'}$ are exactly the eigenvalues of $F_{i,\ell'}\otimes1$ on $V_{i,\ell'}\otimes_{\mathbf Q_{\ell'}}\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$, so $\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is such an eigenvalue by Step 3. By [lem-weil-cohomology-scalar-extension-qlbar], the canonical isomorphism $V_{i,\ell'}\otimes_{\mathbf Q_{\ell'}}\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}=H^i(X,\mathbf Q_{\ell'})\otimes_{\mathbf Q_{\ell'}}\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'})$, where $H^i(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'})$ is the ordinary cohomology group of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] with $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$, carries $F_{i,\ell'}\otimes1$ to the geometric Frobenius on $H^i(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'})$. Conjugate operators have the same eigenvalues, so $\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is an eigenvalue of $F_{i,\ell'}$ on $H^i(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'})$, as the statement asserts.

source.place: statement, 'hence an eigenvalue of $F_{i,\ell'}$ on $H^i(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'})$, the ordinary cohomology group after scalar extension' (the ## Proof gives no argument; written out here)

proof.text: *Step 5: the weight bound for every realization and every complex embedding.* Keep $\ell'$, $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$ and $\jmath_{\ell'}$ as in Step 3, and fix any field isomorphism $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. The situation of [prop-weight-purity], for the prime $\ell'$, the closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$ and this $\iota$, consists of the finite-field datum and the geometric hypotheses on $X_0$, which are those of the present statement, together with the hypotheses that $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ is exceptional-adjoint admissible at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$, that the dualizing Weil complex $(\omega_X,\theta_{\omega_X})$ with its canonical functorial lift exists, and that the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$-cohomology groups are finite-dimensional; these hold by [lem-weil-smooth-proper-purity-hypotheses]. In that situation, [prop-weight-purity-roots] states that every reciprocal root $\gamma\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}$ of $P_{i,\ell'}$ satisfies $|\iota(\gamma)|=q^{i/2}$. By Step 3, $\gamma=\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is such a root, hence $|\iota(\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha))|=q^{i/2}$. Since $\ell'$, $\jmath_{\ell'}$ and $\iota$ were arbitrary, this holds for every prime $\ell'\neq p$, every $\ell'$-adic realization $\jmath_{\ell'}$ and every field isomorphism $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell'}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$.

*Step 6: $\alpha$ is a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$.* Choose one prime $\ell\neq p$ (for instance $\ell=2$ if $p$ is odd and $\ell=3$ if $p=2$) and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. Step 5, applied with $\ell'=\ell$, gives $|\iota(\jmath(\alpha))|=q^{i/2}$ for every $\ell$-adic realization $\jmath:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$ and every field isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. This is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-embedding-extension] for the prime $\ell$, the element $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ and the integer $i$; its conclusion is $|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$ for every embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. Since $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}^{\times}$ by Step 1, $\alpha$ is a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$ in the sense of [def-weil-numbers] (every $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$ restricts to the identity on $\mathbf Q$, so $\operatorname{Emb}_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf Q(\alpha),\mathbf C)$ is the set of all such embeddings).

source.place: ## Proof, '[lem-embedding-extension] extends an arbitrary complex embedding of the number field generated by a root to an isomorphism of algebraic closures. Thus every complex conjugate has absolute value $q^{i/2}$'

proof.text: *Step 7: the ordinary roots.* Let $\beta$ be an ordinary root, that is, $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ for a reciprocal root $\alpha$ (Step 1; equivalently $\beta$ is a root of $P_i$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}$). Then $\mathbf Q(\beta)=\mathbf Q(\alpha)\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}$, and for every embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$ one has $\tau(\beta)=\tau(\alpha)^{-1}$ because $\tau$ is a field homomorphism; hence $|\tau(\beta)|=|\tau(\alpha)|^{-1}=q^{-i/2}$ by Step 6, with the notation of [def-weil-numbers].

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against its master source (identical; slopmaster2's LaTeX version adds a degree clause r_i = dim H^i(X,Q_ℓ), which is prop-integral-recovery's last clause and prop-weil-realization-independent-degrees, and a 'with multiplicity' clause; the master statement is kept). Rewrote the one-paragraph imported proof as seven steps. Dropped prop-integral-recovery from the proof: the statement takes P_i with P_i(0)=1 and P_i^{(ℓ)}=P_{i,ℓ} as hypotheses, so the proof uses only these (the blueprint cited the proposition without using it). Made four hidden arguments into nodes: the reciprocal polynomial P^# = U^r P(U^{-1}) is monic with roots the inverses of the roots (lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial, unsplit, assembled from Mathlib's Polynomial.reverse API); roots are carried along ring homomorphisms (lem-weil-polynomial-root-ring-hom, Mathlib leaf Polynomial.IsRoot.map); the identification H^i(X,Q_ℓ)⊗Q̄_ℓ ≅ H^i(X,Q̄_ℓ) compatible with Frobenius, which the statement's eigenvalue clause needs and which prop-weight-purity only assumes (lem-weil-cohomology-scalar-extension-qlbar, unsplit); and the hypotheses that prop-weight-purity and thm-weil-deligne-purity carry (admissibility of a_X at Q̄_ℓ, the canonical dualizing Weil complex, finite-dimensionality), which no node discharges (lem-weil-smooth-proper-purity-hypotheses, unsplit). Added def-weil-numbers and def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots to stmt_deps (the statement uses 'algebraic integer', 'q-Weil number of weight i', Q(α), the embeddings τ, and the reciprocal-root convention for P_{i,ℓ'}). Each step cites the blueprint sentence it expands; proof_origin is agent (blueprint), since Deligne Weil I (1.6) could not be read here.
